item.title: Beyond the Neighborhood: Multidimensional and Multiscale Sociospatial Change in Dutch Cities
item.dc:title: Beyond the Neighborhood: Multidimensional and Multiscale Sociospatial Change in Dutch Cities
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Urria Ana Petrović Maarten van Ham David Manley a Department of Urbanism, Faculty of Architecture and Built Environment, Delft University of Technology, The Netherlandsb School of Geographical Sciences, University of Bristol, UKIGNACIO URRIA is a PhD Candidate in the Department of Urbanism, Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, Delft University of Technology, 2628 BL Delft, The Netherlands. E-mail: I.A.UrriaYanez@tudelft.nl. His main research interests include sociospatial inequalities, quantitative urban geography, and the measurement and analysis of sociospatial processes across geographical scales and over time.ANA PETROVIĆ is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Urbanism, Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, Delft University of Technology, 2628 BL Delft, The Netherlands. E-mail: A.Petrovic@tudelft.nl. Her research interests include sociospatial inequalities, segregation, and the interaction between people and their urban environment at multiple spatial scales.MAARTEN VAN HAM is a Professor of Urban Geography in the Department of Urbanism, Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, Delft University of Technology, 2628BL Delft, The Netherlands. E-mail: M.vanHam@tudelft.nl. His main research interests are in urban inequality, segregation, and neighborhood effects.DAVID MANLEY is a Professor of Human Geography in the School of Geographical Sciences, Faculty of Science and Engineering, University of Bristol, BS8 1SS Bristol, UK. E-mail: d.manley@bristol.ac.uk. His main research interests are in quantitative data science, neighborhood effects, and social-spatial inequalities.

item.title: The International Dialogue Project: Knowledge in Communication and the Search for Kunskapsvård
item.dc:title: The International Dialogue Project: Knowledge in Communication and the Search for Kunskapsvård
item.dc:creator: Colin Fuchs William Kutz Henrik Gutzon Larsen a Department of Human Geography, Lund University, Swedenb Department of Geography & Environmental Studies, The Open University, UKc Department of Arts and Cultural Sciences, Lund University, SwedenCOLIN FUCHS is a Doctoral Researcher in the Department of Geography & Environmental Studies at The Open University, Milton Keynes MK7 6AA, UK, and a former project assistant in the Department of Human Geography at Lund University. E-mail: colin.fuchs@open.ac.uk. His research interests include the history and philosophy of geography, geographies of knowledge, and the work of Doreen Massey.WILLIAM KUTZ is a Researcher at the Center for Öresund Region Studies, Lund University, 223 62 Lund, Sweden. E-mail: william.kutz@cors.lu.se. His work focuses on the transatlantic circulation of ideas about space and politics since 1945. He also writes about urbanization and housing.HENRIK GUTZON LARSEN is a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Human Geography at Lund University, 223 62 Lund, Sweden. E-mail: henrik_gutzon.larsen@keg.lu.se. His research interests include history of geographic thought, urban geography, and housing.
